chapter.heading: Mordecai’s Advancement
chapter.v:
And King
Ahasuerus imposed tribute on the land and on the islands of the sea.

Now all
the acts of his power and his might, and the account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

For Mordecai
the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, and was great among the Jews and well received by the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his countrymen. [Job 10:18, 19; Jer. 20:14-18]
